title: Start here
text: A small farm, built one working loop at a time. The current plan in one place: start a paper-wick growing trial in New York, then connect and commission the robot in Japan. Start the New York trial → Understand the printed kits Now · NY Grow something this week Garden cress + household paper + water. No robot, sensors, soldering or printed table needed to begin. Next · Japan Commission one care cycle Park the robot. Inspect, measure, make a supervised bottle pour, verify the outcome and recover from interruptions. Later · gated Earn more autonomy Task demonstrations, held-out evaluation, longer observation windows and only then additional care or mobility. What we have decided Topic Current direction Status Watering A small robot-held pouring bottle. Human refill. Chosen; grip/spout and accurate pours untested. Growing Rectangular wicking planter and square covered germination kit. Each can finish a crop. Prints in progress; leak/wick tests pending. Sensing One removable moisture tool; one removable upward-facing light paddle. Selected; thin-paper contact and moving cable need tests. Cameras Use the robot’s head/wrist cameras initially. No separate overhead camera in the first build. Computer The Mac connects to robot interfaces, cameras and ESP32 through the owned powered USB hub. Physical connections still to commission. Furniture Free fully printed modular table for the planters; separate cart for the robot. Table chosen; editable model files still missing. Software Persistent care records, validity checks, restart recovery, exception viewer and replay. Roadmap only; not implemented by this website. Actual planter meshes; conceptual table/robot placement. Bottle spout is a placeholder. Height, reach and structural capacity are untested. The next three useful actions Finish the small planter parts, leak-test and sow cress. Seeds added to the existing cart; purchase is still yours to complete. Download the table’s model files. The ZIP received contains Prusa MINI G-code, not the 13 editable 3MF models. Build the simulated evidence/recovery loop before travel. Physical robot commissioning remains September 30. Removed from V0: electric watering pump, external reservoir, hoses/float switches, scale hardware, separate overhead camera and leak pads. The requested silicone mat, adhesive rubber sheets, plant labels and measuring syringes remain out. Use household measuring materials. This handbook resolves newer decisions over the original deck/redline. “Selected”, “printed”, “connected” and “validated” mean different things; every unresolved fit is listed where it matters. Last consolidated September 22, 2026.

title: Hardware & wiring
text: One Mac. Separate motor and sensor connections. The first build keeps the robot parked and uses its existing cameras. Sensors attach through an ESP32; USB does not power the robot’s motors. The connected workbench The Mac uses the powered hub for USB connections to the robot motor interfaces, existing cameras and ESP32. Robot adapters supply motor power separately; the hub has its own adapter. Equipment shapes and cable routes are illustrative. Open the image for a larger view. The project selected the WowRobo XLeRobot Combo . Recorded kit contents include motor interfaces, three cameras, robot cables and two 12V adapters; verify the delivered boxes and labels. Hub and Anker C300 DC were confirmed bought. The laptop is the current computer plan; no extra Pi is required just to run the sensor logger. Actual macOS drivers, camera bandwidth and robot-software compatibility still need a bench check. Latest cart gap to resolve by reuse: the separate USB-A to USB-C data cable is no longer in the active cart. Have a suitable existing data cable ready for the ESP32; a charge-only cable will not carry readings. The cart’s removal does not prove it was purchased. Likewise, arrange existing cable ties/fasteners/insulation as needed. Each electrical part, in plain language ESP32: the sensor translator A USB data cable connects the powered hub to the ESP32. Sensor records return over USB serial through the hub to the Mac. Open the image for a larger view. One board reads sensors; the three-pack gives spares. The robot’s motor boards do not replace it. Develop and test the serial protocol on the bench before attaching anything to a moving arm. Light: four connections Four connections: verified 3.3V-compatible supply, common ground, SDA data and SCL clock. Actual holder mesh; board geometry and cable routing are illustrative. Open the image for a larger view. Confirm the breakout’s pin labels/supply requirements. Use a 3.3V-compatible bus. Route a flexible four-wire cable to one removable paddle. Test errors through the complete arm motion; long I²C wiring is not automatically reliable. Moisture: local wetness Three connections: switched 3.3V to probe VCC, common ground to GND, and SIG to an ESP32 ADC input. Contact pose is illustrative; depth stop and compliant mounting still need tests. Open the image for a larger view. The SparkFun SEN-13637 measures conductivity, affected by contact and dissolved salts. It is a local wetness proxy, not a reservoir level meter. Keep signal within the ESP32 input range; never feed 5V into its ADC. Relay: briefly power the probe ESP32 output controls module IN; a verified 5V supply powers the module, with common ground. Confirm the delivered module trigger and supply configuration. Open the image for a larger view. Contact side: 3.3V supply at COM, probe VCC at normally open (NO). Separate coil power operates the switch. This is a conceptual mechanism, not an exact model of the purchased relay. Open the image for a larger view. Use one relay channel; no pump is switched. Verify the delivered module’s trigger configuration, supply current and boot-off behavior. Contact side switches 3.3V; relay coil supply is separate. Final GPIOs and power pin selection wait for board pinout verification. These renders explain placement and purpose; the captions preserve functional connections. They are not an approved pin-by-pin harness. Read the board labels and SparkFun hookup guide ; check voltage/continuity before plugging the sensor harness into the computer. The dry assembly bench Start on a dry breadboard, then transfer verified connections to retained connectors/perfboard. One light module and one moisture tool serve the arm; optional air sensing stays off it. Open the image for a larger view. What needs soldering? Part Soldering task What connects afterward ESP32 / BH1750 / optional SHT31 If headers arrive loose, solder the header pins into the board’s plated holes. Already fitted headers need none. Jumper plugs for bench tests; retained connectors for final build. Perfboard + terminal kit Solder headers and screw-terminal pins to perfboard, plus planned interconnects. Strip wire ends and clamp under terminal screws. Screw-terminal moisture probe No solder at the probe terminal if the block arrives fitted. Three wire ends into VCC/GND/SIG. Moving wire splices Only if extending/joining wires that way. Insulate exposed joints with heat-shrink or use suitable enclosed connectors. USB cables, robot kit leads, bottle, planters No added soldering for their ordinary connections. Plug-in or mechanical assembly. Calibration and contact testing Calibration means recording what your installed probe reads on the actual paper with known dry, damp and wet examples. Repeat placements, save the raw range and define valid/ambiguous readings. Do not invent a universal percentage or label voltage as volumetric soil moisture. Contact testing means proving the probe really touches the intended patch consistently without hitting the plastic or crushing the crop. Include “hovering/not touching” trials: they must be INVALID, not interpreted as dry. A compliant printed holder/depth stop helps; software cannot correct a probe that misses the paper. For light, extend the paddle to canopy height, face upward, avoid shadows, stop moving and collect fresh conversions. Start with roughly ten readings over two seconds at default timing, logging median/spread and pose. Reject stale/saturated/bus-error samples. Repeated readings improve repeatability, not absolute calibration; lux is not PPFD. ROHM datasheet . Power and cameras still need commissioning Start from the robot’s supplied wall adapters; check that the actual labels accept Japan’s 100V mains. The owned 288Wh C300 DC is not an already completed motor-power solution: its connector, voltage/current capacity and protection path must match the robot. Do not assume USB-C alone supplies fixed 12V motor power. A fixed overview camera would need its own mount and cable path back to a computer; a mobile robot cannot remain tethered to a fixed camera indefinitely. Our initial choice avoids that extra camera: use the existing head/wrist views and validate that they cover the watering area. No Raspberry Pi, depth camera, scale or pump purchase is required for the initial setup shown here.

title: Shopping list
text: Buy for the current build. Item-by-item purpose, current cart presence and unresolved gaps. A cart is a dated shopping snapshot, not proof of delivery or a complete working robot. Latest readback: September 22, ~11:05 ET. Eleven farm items are active, totaling $126.94 before checkout tax/shipping. One cress packet was added for the NY trial; no purchase was made. Personal items are excluded from this public inventory. Start the trial without waiting for electronics The $4.99 garden-cress packet shows tomorrow morning delivery. Household paper replaces special grow mats for the first batch. The printed parts can be tested on a kitchen surface; the table, robot, probe and ESP32 are not prerequisites for germination. Timing and setup instructions → Representative hardware shapes. Use the item-by-item inventory below for exact products and purchase status. Open the image for a larger view. In the active farm cart Item / Amazon Pack price Decision Purpose / remaining work Organo Republic curled garden cress, 5 g / 2,150 seeds $4.99 ADDED FOR NY TRIAL One packet, delivery displayed September 23, 7–11 AM; not purchased. Start small patches in both kits with household paper. Leave remaining seed in the US. Nalgene 4 oz wide-mouth container $7.00 FIT ISSUE Carries water, but this is a wide-mouth container, not a controlled pouring spout. Measure grip and test a removable spout, or reuse a suitable household bottle before ordering a replacement. 48 MicroMat 4 × 4 inch growing pads $19.58 SUGGEST SKIP Optional for the first crop: the cress creator uses household paper. These pads are smaller than the large tray and currently arrive September 30. Japanese entry treatment of this processed wood-fiber product was not individually confirmed. 22 AWG flexible silicone wire $13.48 KEEP Additional sensor harness for arm movement. Supplied robot motor cables are not spare sensor leads. Route with joint slack and test I²C reliability over the actual light-sensor cable. Three relay modules $8.99 KEEP FOR CURRENT CIRCUIT Use one to switch probe power briefly; two are spares. No pump. Confirm the 5V module supply, 3.3V trigger and boot-off behavior before wiring; a simpler power switch can be evaluated later. Perfboards, headers and screw terminals $13.99 KEEP Secure sensor connections after breadboard tests. Loose headers/terminals need soldering to boards; screw terminals accept the finished wire ends. SparkFun screw-terminal moisture probe $14.45 KEEP / PROTOTYPE One removable arm tool. Reports conductivity as a local wetness proxy, not water depth or calibrated soil water content. Test repeatable contact on thin paper/mat with a depth stop and compliance; leave a seed-free contact patch. Three BH1750 light modules $7.49 KEEP Use ONE movable upward-facing paddle; two spares. Measure at plant height with the arm out of the light path. Lux is not PAR/PPFD. Two SHT31 air sensors $9.99 SUGGEST DEFER Optional temperature/humidity context. If retained, mount one on the robot body or near the table, not on the arm. Breadboard and jumper wires $9.99 KEEP Temporary dry bench wiring before soldering; not a durable exposed arm harness. Three ELEGOO ESP32 boards $16.99 KEEP Use one USB sensor controller; two spares. Supplies sensor readings to the Mac independently of robot motor controllers. Verify delivered board pinout and safe supply voltages. Optional cuts still proposed The growing mats ($19.58, delivery Sep 30) and optional SHT31 air sensor ($9.99) could be deferred, saving $29.57 . That would bring the current farm portion to $97.37 . These removals have not been made by this update. Previously reviewed, now absent from the active cart Absence does not mean “owned.” Reuse what you already have or arrange it locally. The functional USB data cable remains necessary for the ESP32 even though this separate listing is no longer active. Item / Amazon Pack price Decision Purpose / remaining work Two manual mist bottles $5.99 OPTIONAL Hand-wet paper and seeds; reuse a household sprayer if available. Robot trigger actuation has not been demonstrated. AstroAI AM33D multimeter $14.59 BORROW / JAPAN Useful for checking voltage, shorts and wire continuity during assembly; not installed on the robot. ANA does not explicitly clear this meter and pointed leads. Borrow or buy at the destination. M2–M5 screws, nuts and washers $9.99 KEEP IF NO STOCK Useful for sensor holders, not needed to join the selected snap-fit table. Exact holder bolts still depend on measured fit. Carry only useful fasteners; source bundled hex-key tools in Japan unless ANA confirms. Reusable cable straps $4.15 KEEP Retain cables with slack through moving joints; provide strain relief without blocking a camera or pulling on a sensor. Heat-shrink sleeves $6.99 CONDITIONAL Insulate exposed soldered wire splices. Not necessary over enclosed screw terminals. Use local heat tools; no new heat gun is required in this cart. USB-A to USB-C data cable $5.99 KEEP Connects the ESP32 to the owned powered USB hub. The hub connects to the Mac. Already reported / separately arranged Confirmed bought: RSHTECH RSH-ST07 powered hub and Anker C300 DC. Verify actual cable/adapter inventory when assembling. Selected robot package: WowRobo XLeRobot Combo; use the delivered motor adapters/cables/cameras and check against its packing list. Computer and robot cart: Mac and the planned IKEA cart; the printable planter table is separate. Local/reused supplies: paper, clean water, rinse container, kitchen measure, a suitable pouring bottle or fitted spout, solder/stripping tools, small fasteners/retainers/insulation and a borrowed meter. Do we need anything else? No new electronic category is needed to begin the NY grow trial. For the robot, resolve the missing data-cable availability, bottle outlet, probe depth stop/compliance, dry enclosure and cable retention. These are real build dependencies; their absence from the cart must not be mistaken for completion. A grow light depends on measured/observed light at the actual site. Start with a bright location and watch for stretching; don’t buy an arbitrary lamp simply to fill a checklist. The mobile battery harness is still uncommissioned. Use supplied wall power first after label checks. No pump, external tank, scale, overhead camera, leak pads, labels, rubber sheets, silicone mat or measuring syringes are being reintroduced. The current seed packet is for New York; Japan seed remains a local-sourcing task. Prices/delivery can change. Check the actual checkout date before ordering; September 25+ seed arrival is a poor fit for this short pre-trip test. Download item data .

title: Software roadmap
text: Build a care cycle that can explain what happened. The redline feedback becomes an observable, recoverable loop. These are proposed milestones; this site does not implement robot software. Care cycle Evidence Schedule Jev / Astra Release gates Start with plants staying in place 1. Identify and inspect: confirm the tray and a fresh unobstructed view. Open the image for a larger view. 2. Measure and decide: validate readings and contact, then check all care prerequisites. Moisture and light use separate tools. Open the image for a larger view. 3. Supervised care: a small tested pour, with known grip, target and upright recovery. Open the image for a larger view. 4. Verify and park: record the outcome independently and return tools to known rests. Open the image for a larger view. Pause / needs review Any unresolved condition pauses the cycle. On restart, reconcile the physical state before choosing an eligible next step. The feedback’s pick/dock/weigh/dose/return sequence described a broader station design. In our bottle-and-in-place profile, pod handling is explicitly not applicable and scale/pump adapters stay disabled. If we later move pods, reinstate those states with independent grip/location evidence. Before a pour Correct tray identity, fresh camera view, valid measurement/contact, known small fill, verified bottle grip, clear reachable target and a tested upright recovery path. A cloud model cannot override any failed prerequisite. After a pour A motion acknowledgement proves receipt, not water delivery. Record dose as estimated or human-attested unless independently measured. Unknown delivery pauses; never blindly repeat an uncertain pour. Six requirements from the feedback Explicit states: every transition declares evidence, deadline and recovery action. Persistent actions: save cycle/command IDs and INTENDED, ATTEMPTED and VERIFIED separately. Duplicate requests return existing records. A crash during possible watering leaves UNKNOWN until reconciled. Valid sensors: freshness, calibrated range, contact, camera coverage and quality flags are action prerequisites. Shared evidence: link tray, recipe, images, readings, actions, interventions and all relevant versions in one exportable incident. Exception viewer: show the latest image, its age, current action, last verified state and eligible recovery choices. Disable a watering retry when delivery is unknown. Fault replay: simulate interruptions now; retain real failures as regressions later. Minimal proposed evidence record { "cycle_id": "...", "command_id": "...", "tray_id": "A", "source": "simulation | hardware", "recipe_version": "...", "time": "...", "images": [{"id": "...", "captured_at": "..."}], "readings": [{"value": 0, "unit": "raw_adc", "validity": "INVALID_CONTACT", "calibration_id": "..."}], "action": "water", "state": "INTENDED", "delivery": "not_attempted | unknown | human_attested | measured", "software_version": "...", "policy_version": "...", "interventions": [] } SQLite plus image files is the proposed local record store. Command IDs alone cannot guarantee exactly-once physical watering. Preserve original images and keep simulation evidence distinct from hardware evidence. Software now; robot commissioning September 30 Window Deliverable Gate Sep 22–24 Capability profile, event schema, simulator, durable action records, initial exception viewer. Run the separate NY grow trial. Interrupt every simulated state; no duplicate or uncertain repeat watering. Sep 25–26 Fault replay, sensor validity, camera spill cases, Jev shadow adapter. Stale/hidden view, wrong identity, missing contact, uncertain grip, dropped ACK and cloud loss are handled. Sep 27–29 Freeze crop recipe, export/restore, offline rehearsal and packaging. Recover evidence and resolve a defined exception through the viewer. NY seedlings remain with local care or are cleaned up. Sep 30–Oct 2 · D1–3 Hardware adapters, calibration, dummy-tray recovery, moving cable sweeps and small hand/teleop bottle pours. Measure real fits, prove safe state-dependent stops and contact validity; do not infer delivered volume from tilt. Oct 3–5 · D4–6 Supervised parked cycles at every intended tray position; collect demonstrations once teleop is reliable. All outcomes and interventions recorded. No unobserved watering authority. Oct 6–8 · D7–9 Feature freeze; progressive 2-hour, then 8-hour, then 24-hour observation/alert windows, with human watering arranged. Relevant faults pass first. Autonomous watering requires a separate validated delivery/recovery profile. Oct 9–10 · D10–11 Repeat weak cases, restore backups, export dataset and caretaker handoff. Caretaker can resolve representative exceptions. Navigation remains conditional. Dates are targets, not evidence of completion. A failed gate holds the previous operating level. The NY growing trial is newly in scope; earlier statements that no physical work happens until September 30 now apply to robot commissioning, not planter tests. Jev classifies; Astra investigates; local checks decide eligibility Software concept on the existing Mac; no additional computer is implied. Local checks collect evidence, Jev classifies in shadow mode, Astra investigates exceptions, and a person reviews proposals. Local eligibility checks remain in charge; outcomes need independent verification. Open the image for a larger view. Jev categories: normal, needs reinspection, handling fault, watering discrepancy, crop concern and unknown. Begin in shadow mode with no actuation permission. The redline’s 0.85 heuristic is not a validated threshold, and the described helper source has not been audited here. Compare rules and Jev on the same evidence: missed faults, false clearances, unnecessary alerts, review time, latency and cost. Independently label outcomes and hold out episodes from tuning. The suggested 120 labelled episodes / at least 10 per priority fault class is a starting collection target, not a reliability guarantee. Astra may propose changes and experiments. Version and evaluate them before a bounded supervised trial; retain rollback. Automatic code modification/retraining and complex orchestration are deferred. Spill checks and failure recovery Camera spill status is CLEAR / SPILL / UNKNOWN. Hidden, dark, stale, glare-obscured or out-of-frame areas are UNKNOWN. Dedicated leak pads were removed at your request; vision remains experimental. If a pour must stop, execute the commissioned return-upright action when control is available. Do not blindly release or de-energize a tilted bottle. Total power loss may leave it draining; small starting fills and household containment matter. Do not claim camera software alone prevents damage. Every release replays accumulated failures. Hardware changes trigger the relevant real tests again. Mobile navigation, automatic refill, printer part pickup and construction tasks remain outside the first dependable parked loop. What upstream already provides Detailed roadmap companion

Verify and park: record the outcome independently and return tools to known rests. Open the image for a larger view. Pause / needs review Any unresolved condition pauses the cycle. On restart, reconcile the physical state before choosing an eligible next step. The feedback’s pick/dock/weigh/dose/return sequence described a broader station design. In our bottle-and-in-place profile, pod handling is explicitly not applicable and scale/pump adapters stay disabled. If we later move pods, reinstate those states with independent grip/location evidence. Before a pour Correct tray identity, fresh camera view, valid measurement/contact, known small fill, verified bottle grip, clear reachable target and a tested upright recovery path. A cloud model cannot override any failed prerequisite. After a pour A motion acknowledgement proves receipt, not water delivery. Record dose as estimated or human-attested unless independently measured. Unknown delivery pauses; never blindly repeat an uncertain pour.

title: Six requirements from the feedback
text: Six requirements from the feedback Explicit states: every transition declares evidence, deadline and recovery action. Persistent actions: save cycle/command IDs and INTENDED, ATTEMPTED and VERIFIED separately. Duplicate requests return existing records. A crash during possible watering leaves UNKNOWN until reconciled. Valid sensors: freshness, calibrated range, contact, camera coverage and quality flags are action prerequisites. Shared evidence: link tray, recipe, images, readings, actions, interventions and all relevant versions in one exportable incident. Exception viewer: show the latest image, its age, current action, last verified state and eligible recovery choices. Disable a watering retry when delivery is unknown. Fault replay: simulate interruptions now; retain real failures as regressions later. Minimal proposed evidence record { "cycle_id": "...", "command_id": "...", "tray_id": "A", "source": "simulation | hardware", "recipe_version": "...", "time": "...", "images": [{"id": "...", "captured_at": "..."}], "readings": [{"value": 0, "unit": "raw_adc", "validity": "INVALID_CONTACT", "calibration_id": "..."}], "action": "water", "state": "INTENDED", "delivery": "not_attempted | unknown | human_attested | measured", "software_version": "...", "policy_version": "...", "interventions": [] } SQLite plus image files is the proposed local record store. Command IDs alone cannot guarantee exactly-once physical watering. Preserve original images and keep simulation evidence distinct from hardware evidence.

title: Software now; robot commissioning September 30
text: Software now; robot commissioning September 30 Window Deliverable Gate Sep 22–24 Capability profile, event schema, simulator, durable action records, initial exception viewer. Run the separate NY grow trial. Interrupt every simulated state; no duplicate or uncertain repeat watering. Sep 25–26 Fault replay, sensor validity, camera spill cases, Jev shadow adapter. Stale/hidden view, wrong identity, missing contact, uncertain grip, dropped ACK and cloud loss are handled. Sep 27–29 Freeze crop recipe, export/restore, offline rehearsal and packaging. Recover evidence and resolve a defined exception through the viewer. NY seedlings remain with local care or are cleaned up. Measure real fits, prove safe state-dependent stops and contact validity; do not infer delivered volume from tilt. Autonomous watering requires a separate validated delivery/recovery profile. Oct 9–10 · D10–11 Repeat weak cases, restore backups, export dataset and caretaker handoff. Caretaker can resolve representative exceptions. Navigation remains conditional. Dates are targets, not evidence of completion. A failed gate holds the previous operating level. The NY growing trial is newly in scope; earlier statements that no physical work happens until September 30 now apply to robot commissioning, not planter tests.

title: Jev classifies; Astra investigates; local checks decide eligibility

title: Spill checks and failure recovery
text: Spill checks and failure recovery Camera spill status is CLEAR / SPILL / UNKNOWN. Hidden, dark, stale, glare-obscured or out-of-frame areas are UNKNOWN. Do not blindly release or de-energize a tilted bottle. Total power loss may leave it draining; small starting fills and household containment matter. title: Japan & carry-on
text: Bring the experiment, not a live crop. Carry-on only, ANA. Use the New York week for evidence; start a fresh local crop after arrival. Clean, dry prints and an empty bottle only. The render is not a packing clearance or size guarantee; follow the item-specific travel notes below. Open the image for a larger view. Pack / source / verify Category Plan Reason Printed kits and dry electronics Clean, dry and protect; keep connections identified. Remove growing material and water. Protect sensor ends and loose battery terminals. Seed and used paper / soil / plants NY test stays in the US; buy Japan seed locally. Japan plant quarantine regulates seeds/plants and prohibits soil. We have not obtained import documents. Bottles Pack empty. Refill after arrival; do not carry irrigation water. Pointed soldering iron and hand tools Borrow / buy in Japan. ANA explicitly excludes pointed soldering irons and broadly restricts tools in carry-on. Multimeter and pointed probes Borrow / buy in Japan unless ANA confirms the exact kit. No explicit ANA classification was found. This is uncertainty, not proof every meter is banned. Anker C300 DC, 288Wh Destination power equipment; do not pack for this passenger flight. Exceeds the normal passenger lithium-battery limits. Being owned does not establish motor wiring compatibility. Growing mats Optional. Use household paper for NY; source locally if needed later. Current cart delivery Sep 30 misses the NY trial. Exact processed wood-fiber customs treatment was not individually cleared. title: Growing trial & kits
text: Two printed kits. One growing trial. Understand the water paths, set up the kits, and follow the New York cress trial in one place. Keep the crop in the kit you sowed it in; transplanting is not required. Wicking planter Square kit Robot access NY timing Setup Daily care Troubleshooting Notebook Rectangular self-watering cress planter 6 printed pieces What each piece does Trough: stores the small supply of water. Holder: supports the growing paper above it. Four insets: hold paper down into water and make wick paths. They are not four separate crop pots. Trough envelope from the downloaded STL: approximately 180 × 85 × 25 mm. Paper and water are not printed parts. Capillary action does the work A continuous sheet of paper carries water from the trough to the seed platform. Four insets keep the paper in contact with water. Refill before the wick loses contact. Passive watering reduces intervention; it does not guarantee the planter can be left alone for six days. Actual creator meshes cut open for explanation. Household paper connects the seed platform to the stored water; the four insets are wick holders. The cutaway is not a print file. Open the image for a larger view. Original by Macce · CC BY-SA 4.0 . The creator uses household paper and printed PETG; our PLA version needs its own leak and durability checks. Follow the start guide . Square germination tray kit Original downloaded meshes, separated in Blender to explain their roles. Cover orientation depends on its intended use; use it over the growing insert for early germination. Part Function Downloaded envelope A · Cover / part 3 Retains humidity and blocks light initially; remove for the green growth stage. Weighted blackout is crop-specific and not needed for our first cress trial. 205 × 205 × 35 mm B · Insert / part 2 Holds medium/seeds; perforations provide drainage/root access. 195 × 195 × 35 mm C · Outer tray / part 1 Supports the insert and catches or holds water. 220 × 220 × 50 mm These measured STL bounds differ from the listing’s nominal dimensions. Use the downloaded dimensions for print planning. Seed on a suitable moist medium in B; C is not a signal to flood the seeds. If there is an air gap to bottom water, top-wet initially and verify the medium’s water path. Original by HomestteadAce · CC BY-SA 4.0 . Both kits can stay on an ordinary stable household surface for the New York trial. How the robot joins this later Recognize the tray and the saved watering target while its base is parked. Inspect the uncovered crop and test an unseeded moisture patch without digging through roots. Use one removable light paddle at plant height as a separate operation. Take a small bottle, pour a tested amount at an accessible target and return upright. Observe wetness/spills and save evidence. Uncertain delivery pauses the cycle. Manual lid removal, bottle refill and tool loading are acceptable V0 steps. The cress refill hole is narrow; the square tray’s access around its fitted insert also needs physical testing. Neither a render nor the upstream demo proves these targets are reachable with our bottle. Why a water pocket if the robot waters? The pocket is inside the planter; the robot can refill it. We removed the separate powered irrigation system, not the plant’s ability to hold water. The timing works if we start promptly Seed packet added: Organo Republic curled garden cress, 5 g / 2,150 seeds, $4.99 , quantity one. Amazon displayed September 23, 7–11 AM in the cart on September 22. Not purchased; recheck delivery at checkout. Seed arrival tomorrow + prompt plate changes leaves roughly 4–5 growing days before a six-days-away departure. Garden cress ( Lepidium sativum ) suits a small paper-based trial. A seed supplier gives roughly 2–4 days to germinate and 7–10 days to harvest ; real timing varies. By departure, look for emerging roots, shoots and opening seed leaves. Seedmart’s cress guide . This timeline is our planning estimate, not a guarantee for the packet in the cart. Printing: Creality reports the outer tray completed September 22 at 11:23. The original cover job was stopped and replaced with one seven-part plate: the square insert plus all six cress-planter pieces (274.84 g, sliced estimate 10h06m). Creality accepted the replacement September 22 with calibration enabled. The dedicated square cover is deferred; use a loose household cover initially. Both kits can be functionally ready after this job finishes and cools, subject to print quality and a leak test. If prints slip, sow a separate small reference patch in a kitchen dish; don’t wait for the table. Do not transplant an established rooted paper sheet merely to meet the schedule. Purchase cutoff: tomorrow delivery leaves a useful trial. Arrival September 25 or later gives much less time; if checkout slips that far, skip this online order for the pre-trip test and source seeds locally. The $19.58 growing mats show September 30 delivery and are unnecessary for this trial. Your first setup, step by step Use what you already have Completed printed cress planter, or the square kit. Fresh garden-cress seed. Use untreated seed intended for growing; check the delivered packet. Plain, unscented household kitchen paper and clean water. A clean kitchen tray/dish underneath, a small cup or spoon, and a phone camera. A household loose cover if the cress planter needs humidity retention; square kit includes its cover. No growing soil, fertilizer, purchased mats, sensors or robot needed for this short paper trial. What “self-watering” means The rectangular planter stores a little water below the seeds. Paper carries it upward by capillary action. You still check it and refill by hand. The square kit has a cover and removable insert, but it does not automatically wick unless its growing medium makes the needed connection to water. See the planter renders Inspect, rinse and leak-test Remove loose plastic, rinse with cool water and check the fit without forcing clips. Put the empty trough/outer tray on dry kitchen paper inside an existing dish. Add a modest amount of water below the growing surface. Inspect after 30 minutes and again later that day. Any wet patch underneath fails the test: use another dish for growing while repairing/reprinting. The 30-minute check is our proposed initial screen, not a leak certification. PLA prints may retain residue and are not established food-contact equipment. Treat unknown-filament prints as growth/mechanical tests; use a suitable food-growing container for any batch intended to eat. Avoid boiling water or a hot dishwasher on the PLA parts. Make the wick actually touch the water For the rectangular planter: snap its four insets into the holder. Feed paper down into each inset and lay 3–4 layers across the seed platform, maintaining a continuous wet-paper path. Pre-wet the paper, drain surface puddles and fill the trough below the seed platform. The creator suggests about 80% full; don’t use that as an excuse to submerge seeds. For the square kit: put damp paper on the perforated insert inside its outer tray. Keep it moist from above initially; only rely on bottom water after confirming paper/root contact or a working wick. Water underneath an air gap cannot wet the paper automatically. Sow a small, even patch Scatter dry cress seeds onto moist paper, with no thick piles. Do not pre-soak cress: it becomes sticky when wet. One packet is enough for small test patches; there is no need to densely fill the entire large tray. Give both kits similar seeded patch areas and density, using the same seed lot. Keep an unseeded edge on the same sheet for moisture checks. Use a phone note or tape already at home to label A = wick planter, B = square tray, and optionally C = household dish. A household reference can help distinguish seed trouble from a printed-container problem; it is not a controlled scientific experiment. Keep the first stage damp, then give it light Follow the seed packet’s conditions. A loose cover can reduce early drying; check at least morning and evening and do not seal it airtight. Remove the cover when shoots emerge and begin standing up; use the plant’s condition rather than an automatic date. Then place it in bright natural light away from intense window heat, radiators and cold drafts. An ordinary comfortable room is a practical starting point. Leave airflow around the seedlings. Never leave a covered tray baking in direct sun. Assembly steps adapted from Macce’s planter instructions ; cress sowing/early growth from Seedmart . Our leak screens, comparisons and log schedule are proposed tests. The tray setup is an adaptation to the actual printed kit, not a claim that the seed supplier tested these prints. Illustrative observations, not a promised timetable. Log what your crop actually does. Open the image for a larger view. A six-day observation plan Day 0 · fit, water and sow Complete the leak/wick checks, photograph the dry assembly and first sowing. Record crop, date, paper layers, seeded area and starting water level. Measure water with kitchen utensils only if practical; otherwise record “not measured”. Days 1–2 · check the water path Morning and evening: check the trough, paper at several spots, and the dry surface underneath. Add only enough water to keep paper evenly damp. Photograph from the same angle. Some seed may swell or begin rooting; slower emergence is still possible. Days 2–4 · look for emergence When shoots establish, uncover and give bright light. Log first roots, upright shoots and seed leaves. If a patch is dry while the trough has water, fix wick contact instead of adding more water blindly. Days 4–5 · test useful repeatability Compare wetness across the tray, count manual top-ups and note any leak or wilt. Practice tiny hand pours at the refill opening using your kitchen measure. Do not deliberately drought-stress the live crop; test dry/damp/wet sensor samples separately if electronics are available. Day 6 · record and close the trial Take final photos, compare the two kits, list changes for Japan and export the notebook. Arrange continued human care in New York or end the trial and clean/dry the prints. Do not pack live seedlings, used growing medium or remaining seed for Japan under an assumption that they are cleared. Success before departure: visible germination, a reliable water path, no observed leaks, a known manual refill routine and photos/notes explaining failures. This does not establish autonomous care, edible-product safety or a guaranteed number of unattended days. What a problem looks like There is water below, but the paper is dry The paper may not reach the reservoir, the wick may have separated, or the tray may be tilted. Re-wet and reconnect it. Check multiple points. Don’t drown the seeds to compensate for an air gap. Seeds are floating or the surface is puddled Remove excess water gently and lower the water level. Keep the paper damp, not submerged. Avoid blasting seeds with a direct pour. The shoots are pale or leaning Uncover after emergence and improve light without overheating. Use the same camera angle to track changes; brightness in a phone photo alone is not a light-meter reading. Nothing has emerged by day 4 Check seed identity/packet guidance, freshness, paper moisture and temperature. Compare the household reference if you started one. Don’t keep increasing water; saturated seeds can also fail. Slime, fuzzy growth or an unpleasant smell Cress produces clear gel around wet seeds. Root hairs can look fuzzy, while spreading fuzzy patches, discoloration or a bad smell warrant stopping and discarding the affected trial. A photo alone may not distinguish them reliably. Don’t eat an uncertain batch; clean the container before restarting. Your trial notebook Checks and observations stay in this browser. They are not uploaded, synced, or sent to the robot. Export before changing devices or clearing browser storage. text: The timing works if we start promptly Seed packet added: Organo Republic curled garden cress, 5 g / 2,150 seeds, $4.99 , quantity one. Amazon displayed September 23, 7–11 AM in the cart on September 22. Not purchased; recheck delivery at checkout. Seed arrival tomorrow + prompt plate changes leaves roughly 4–5 growing days before a six-days-away departure. Garden cress ( Lepidium sativum ) suits a small paper-based trial. A seed supplier gives roughly 2–4 days to germinate and 7–10 days to harvest ; real timing varies. By departure, look for emerging roots, shoots and opening seed leaves. Seedmart’s cress guide . This timeline is our planning estimate, not a guarantee for the packet in the cart. Printing: Creality reports the outer tray completed September 22 at 11:23. The original cover job was stopped and replaced with one seven-part plate: the square insert plus all six cress-planter pieces (274.84 g, sliced estimate 10h06m). Creality accepted the replacement September 22 with calibration enabled. The dedicated square cover is deferred; use a loose household cover initially. Both kits can be functionally ready after this job finishes and cools, subject to print quality and a leak test. If prints slip, sow a separate small reference patch in a kitchen dish; don’t wait for the table. Do not transplant an established rooted paper sheet merely to meet the schedule. Purchase cutoff: tomorrow delivery leaves a useful trial. Arrival September 25 or later gives much less time; if checkout slips that far, skip this online order for the pre-trip test and source seeds locally. The $19.58 growing mats show September 30 delivery and are unnecessary for this trial.

title: Your first setup, step by step
text: Your first setup, step by step Use what you already have Completed printed cress planter, or the square kit. Fresh garden-cress seed. Use untreated seed intended for growing; check the delivered packet. Plain, unscented household kitchen paper and clean water. A clean kitchen tray/dish underneath, a small cup or spoon, and a phone camera. A household loose cover if the cress planter needs humidity retention; square kit includes its cover. No growing soil, fertilizer, purchased mats, sensors or robot needed for this short paper trial. What “self-watering” means The rectangular planter stores a little water below the seeds. Paper carries it upward by capillary action. You still check it and refill by hand. The square kit has a cover and removable insert, but it does not automatically wick unless its growing medium makes the needed connection to water. See the planter renders Inspect, rinse and leak-test Remove loose plastic, rinse with cool water and check the fit without forcing clips. Put the empty trough/outer tray on dry kitchen paper inside an existing dish. Add a modest amount of water below the growing surface. Inspect after 30 minutes and again later that day. Any wet patch underneath fails the test: use another dish for growing while repairing/reprinting. The 30-minute check is our proposed initial screen, not a leak certification. PLA prints may retain residue and are not established food-contact equipment. Treat unknown-filament prints as growth/mechanical tests; use a suitable food-growing container for any batch intended to eat. Avoid boiling water or a hot dishwasher on the PLA parts. Make the wick actually touch the water For the rectangular planter: snap its four insets into the holder. Feed paper down into each inset and lay 3–4 layers across the seed platform, maintaining a continuous wet-paper path. Pre-wet the paper, drain surface puddles and fill the trough below the seed platform. The creator suggests about 80% full; don’t use that as an excuse to submerge seeds. For the square kit: put damp paper on the perforated insert inside its outer tray. Keep it moist from above initially; only rely on bottom water after confirming paper/root contact or a working wick. Water underneath an air gap cannot wet the paper automatically. Sow a small, even patch Scatter dry cress seeds onto moist paper, with no thick piles. Do not pre-soak cress: it becomes sticky when wet. One packet is enough for small test patches; there is no need to densely fill the entire large tray. Give both kits similar seeded patch areas and density, using the same seed lot. Keep an unseeded edge on the same sheet for moisture checks. Use a phone note or tape already at home to label A = wick planter, B = square tray, and optionally C = household dish. A household reference can help distinguish seed trouble from a printed-container problem; it is not a controlled scientific experiment. Keep the first stage damp, then give it light Follow the seed packet’s conditions. A loose cover can reduce early drying; check at least morning and evening and do not seal it airtight. Remove the cover when shoots emerge and begin standing up; use the plant’s condition rather than an automatic date. Then place it in bright natural light away from intense window heat, radiators and cold drafts. An ordinary comfortable room is a practical starting point. Leave airflow around the seedlings. Never leave a covered tray baking in direct sun. Assembly steps adapted from Macce’s planter instructions ; cress sowing/early growth from Seedmart . Our leak screens, comparisons and log schedule are proposed tests. The tray setup is an adaptation to the actual printed kit, not a claim that the seed supplier tested these prints.

title: A six-day observation plan
text: Illustrative observations, not a promised timetable. Log what your crop actually does. Open the image for a larger view. A six-day observation plan Day 0 · fit, water and sow Complete the leak/wick checks, photograph the dry assembly and first sowing. Record crop, date, paper layers, seeded area and starting water level. Measure water with kitchen utensils only if practical; otherwise record “not measured”. Days 1–2 · check the water path Morning and evening: check the trough, paper at several spots, and the dry surface underneath. Add only enough water to keep paper evenly damp. Photograph from the same angle. Some seed may swell or begin rooting; slower emergence is still possible. Days 2–4 · look for emergence When shoots establish, uncover and give bright light. Log first roots, upright shoots and seed leaves. If a patch is dry while the trough has water, fix wick contact instead of adding more water blindly. Days 4–5 · test useful repeatability Compare wetness across the tray, count manual top-ups and note any leak or wilt. Practice tiny hand pours at the refill opening using your kitchen measure. Do not deliberately drought-stress the live crop; test dry/damp/wet sensor samples separately if electronics are available. Day 6 · record and close the trial Take final photos, compare the two kits, list changes for Japan and export the notebook. Arrange continued human care in New York or end the trial and clean/dry the prints. Do not pack live seedlings, used growing medium or remaining seed for Japan under an assumption that they are cleared. Success before departure: visible germination, a reliable water path, no observed leaks, a known manual refill routine and photos/notes explaining failures. This does not establish autonomous care, edible-product safety or a guaranteed number of unattended days.

title: What a problem looks like
text: What a problem looks like There is water below, but the paper is dry The paper may not reach the reservoir, the wick may have separated, or the tray may be tilted. Re-wet and reconnect it. Check multiple points. Don’t drown the seeds to compensate for an air gap. Seeds are floating or the surface is puddled Remove excess water gently and lower the water level. Keep the paper damp, not submerged. Avoid blasting seeds with a direct pour. The shoots are pale or leaning Uncover after emergence and improve light without overheating. Use the same camera angle to track changes; brightness in a phone photo alone is not a light-meter reading. Nothing has emerged by day 4 Check seed identity/packet guidance, freshness, paper moisture and temperature. Compare the household reference if you started one. Don’t keep increasing water; saturated seeds can also fail. Slime, fuzzy growth or an unpleasant smell Cress produces clear gel around wet seeds. Root hairs can look fuzzy, while spreading fuzzy patches, discoloration or a bad smell warrant stopping and discarding the affected trial. A photo alone may not distinguish them reliably. Don’t eat an uncertain batch; clean the container before restarting.
